name: Switchblade 300

placement_rationale.text: 5 km marks the squad/platoon launch position, not a strike range — Switchblade 300 is backpack-portable and hand-launched, so its reach is whatever an infantry unit can carry it to, and no flight-range figure is recorded in this asset's own characteristics beyond its ~15-minute endurance class. Sitting at the outer edge of doctrine.md §2's 0–10 km FPV-strike-range band and just past the 1–5 km close-reconnaissance band, 5 km is a plausible depth for a squad/platoon-level launch point rather than a position standing directly on the zero line. Because this is man-portable rather than antenna/relay-dependent equipment, it doesn't carry the deeper 8–10 km launch-team offset doctrine.md describes for RU-side FPV teams with fixed control equipment.

cost.display: Donated (unit cost historically cited around $6,000-70,000 depending on generation/source)

characteristics: Strength: Man-portable at squad/platoon level, giving small units organic precision strike without waiting for a supporting asset
Limitation: Very short range and endurance compared to larger loitering munitions like Lancet
Estimated quantity available: Delivered in the low thousands across multiple aid packages; exact current total not disclosed
employment_notes: Represents the U.S. donation of loitering munitions specifically to push precision-strike capability down to the smallest tactical units
contrast_vs_traditional: A man-portable loitering munition puts precision-strike capability traditionally reserved for artillery or air support directly in an infantry squad's hands — the doctrine.md finding that kill chains are now distributed down to squad level rather than concentrated at higher HQ, made literal as a piece of individual-unit equipment.

connections.description: Receives target cueing from a tactical reconnaissance drone before launch — the same recon-to-strike pairing HIMARS and M777 rely on, at squad range instead of battery range.

notes: Rests only on tertiary reference works; wants a primary or trade source.
